name: Ameriquest

summary.text: Ameriquest was an Orange County, California subprime mortgage lender, described by the California Attorney General in 2006 as the nation's largest sub-prime lender. On January 23, 2006 attorneys general and lending regulators from 49 states announced a $325 million settlement with Ameriquest resolving predatory lending allegations, of which $295 million was earmarked for consumer restitution; its parent ACC Capital Holdings agreed to change business practices without acknowledging wrongdoing, and its practices were to be independently monitored. Investigators cited inadequate disclosure of prepayment penalties and loan terms, inflated appraisals and misrepresented credit ratings.

facts.claim: On January 23, 2006 California Attorney General Bill Lockyer announced a $325 million, 49-state settlement with Ameriquest resolving predatory lending allegations against what the office called the nation's largest sub-prime lender; $295 million was earmarked for consumer restitution with the remainder tied to reforms and enforcement costs.

facts.claim: Investigators' findings behind the settlement included inadequate disclosure of prepayment penalties, discount points and other loan terms, inflated appraisals and misrepresented credit ratings; New York's Attorney General said salespeople concealed interest-rate and loan costs and pressured appraisers.
facts.quote: Investigators' findings included inadequate disclosure of prepayment penalties, discount points and other loan terms, along with inflated appraisals and misrepresented credit ratings.

facts.claim: Ameriquest's parent, ACC Capital Holdings, agreed to change certain business practices without acknowledging wrongdoing, and the company's practices were to be independently monitored to ensure compliance.
facts.quote: Its practices will be independently monitored to ensure the company complies.

facts.claim: The settlement followed more than two years of investigation by state attorneys general, lending regulators and local prosecutors and more than a year of negotiation; Virginia was excluded because Ameriquest did not lend there, and the wholesale affiliate Argent Mortgage was not a party.
facts.quote: It culminated more than two years of investigation by the Attorneys General, state lending regulators and local prosecutors, and more than one year of settlement negotiations.

facts.claim: At the time the Ameriquest settlement was described as the second-largest consumer protection settlement in U.S. history, after the $484 million predatory lending agreement reached in 2002 with Household Finance Corp.
facts.quote: It is the second-largest consumer protection settlement in U.S. history, following the $484 million predatory lending agreement reached in 2002 with Household Finance Corp.

openQuestions: Site claim that Ameriquest was part of a 'subprime fraud conveyor' with originators paid upfront commissions and 'systematic fabrication of W-2s': the 2006 settlement documents inadequate disclosure, inflated appraisals and misrepresented credit ratings, not W-2 fabrication; the commission structure was not covered.

Founder Roland Arnall's role and his later appointment as U.S. ambassador to the Netherlands were not confirmed by any source returned; the owner should check the FCIC report or Senate Foreign Relations records.
Ameriquest's wind-down and the 2007 sale of its servicing business were not researched.
